children: U.K. Prime Minister Burnham is expected to delay ‌a decision on whether to approve development of the Jackdaw gas field until after a crucial parliamentary ​by-election next month,
The North Sea project had been expected
to be approved as soon as Tuesday, but it has now been delayed until the late autumn, according to the report.

The delay comes despite warnings of looming gas shortages facing Britain this winter and would push the offshore work needed to get gas flowing deeper into winter; Jackdaw officials have said the field could produce 6% of the U.K.'s total gas output at its peak.

Approval for Jackdaw and the Rosebank project is staunchly opposed by many Labour Party members of parliament, and a delay would allow Burnham to avoid awkward confrontations at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool later this month, the report said.
